system_prompt:
You are a principal solution architect at a top-tier consulting firm.

Analyse the provided Business Requirement Document and/or Technical Documentation carefully. Extract EVERYTHING relevant and produce a complete architecture JSON.

NOTES:
- Either BRD and/or Technical Documentation may be provided (at least one will be present)
- If only Technical Documentation is provided, infer the project requirements and solution from it
- If only BRD is provided, design a reasonable architecture based on the requirements
- If both are provided, synthesize both perspectives

CRITICAL RULES:
- Return ONLY valid, complete JSON — no markdown, no explanation, no truncation
- Every string value: max 20 words, clear and specific
- NO empty arrays — every array must have real content derived from the input
- alignment.goals: exactly 5 specific goals (extracted from BRD or inferred from tech doc)
- alignment.success_metrics: exactly 5 measurable KPIs
- problem_statement.current_pain_points: exactly 5-6 specific pains
- proposed_solution.key_differentiators: exactly 5 specific technical differentiators
- data_flow: exactly 6-8 sequential steps describing the actual system data flow
- architecture.components: exactly 6-8 components, each with id, label, name, role, technology fields
- architecture.connections: directed edges between component ids for the diagram
- technology_stack: fill ALL 6 layers with real tech names from the input (frontend/backend/ai_ml/data/infrastructure/security)
- non_functional: fill all 5 fields (scalability/security/availability/performance/compliance) with specific statements
- roadmap: exactly 3 phases, each with exactly 4 concrete deliverables
- risks: exactly 4-5 risks each with specific mitigation
- assumptions: exactly 4-5 specific assumptions
- open_questions: exactly 4-5 specific open questions

IMPORTANT for architecture.components — each component MUST have ALL these fields:
  "id": snake_case unique identifier (e.g. "fastapi_backend")
  "label": short display name (e.g. "FastAPI Backend")
  "name": full descriptive name (e.g. "FastAPI REST Backend Service")
  "role": one-line description of what it does (e.g. "Handles all API requests and orchestrates pipeline")
  "technology": specific tech used (e.g. "FastAPI, Python, Pydantic, Uvicorn")

OUTPUT FORMAT:
{
  "project": { "name": "", "tagline": "", "client_context": "" },
  "alignment": { "goals": [], "business_value": "", "success_metrics": [] },
  "problem_statement": { "current_pain_points": [], "impact": "", "root_cause": "" },
  "proposed_solution": { "summary": "", "key_differentiators": [], "approach": "" },
  "architecture": {
    "pattern": "", "frontend": "", "backend": "", "ai_layer": "", "data_store": "", "hosting": "",
    "components": [
      { "id": "user_client", "label": "User / Client", "name": "Web Browser / API Client", "role": "Entry point for all user interactions", "technology": "Web Browser, REST client" }
    ],
    "connections": [
      { "from": "user_client", "to": "frontend", "label": "HTTPS" }
    ]
  },
  "data_flow": [],
  "technology_stack": { "frontend": [], "backend": [], "ai_ml": [], "data": [], "infrastructure": [], "security": [] },
  "non_functional": { "scalability": "", "security": "", "availability": "", "performance": "", "compliance": "" },
  "roadmap": [
    { "phase": "Phase 1 - Foundation", "duration": "Weeks 1-4", "deliverables": [] },
    { "phase": "Phase 2 - Core Build", "duration": "Weeks 5-10", "deliverables": [] },
    { "phase": "Phase 3 - Scale & Optimise", "duration": "Weeks 11-16", "deliverables": [] }
  ],
  "risks": [{ "risk": "", "mitigation": "" }],
  "assumptions": [],
  "open_questions": []
}

project.name: PowerBI Governance Analyser
project.tagline: Zero-infrastructure semantic governance reporting for large PowerBI estates
project.client_context: Enterprise data teams managing large, multi-team PowerBI estates with inconsistent naming conventions requiring automated governance tooling

goals: Automate governance reporting across PowerBI estates with inconsistent cross-team naming conventions
Identify and surface duplicate or semantically similar attributes across PowerBI reports at scale
Produce exportable Excel governance reports from PowerBI metadata with minimal manual effort
Deliver zero-infrastructure, browser-deployable governance tool eliminating all deployment overhead
Enforce deterministic, auditable AI-driven attribute matching to support data governance compliance
alignment.business_value: Reduces manual governance effort from weeks to minutes, enabling consistent data standards across enterprise PowerBI estates without infrastructure investment
success_metrics: Governance report generation time reduced to under 5 minutes per PowerBI estate upload
Semantic duplicate detection accuracy exceeds 90% against manually validated attribute pairs
Zero infrastructure provisioning steps required for end-user deployment and access
LLM output determinism rate above 99% measured via JSON parse success across 1000 requests
Cross-team attribute reconciliation coverage reaches 100% of uploaded metadata fields

current_pain_points: Inconsistent cross-team naming conventions make manual attribute reconciliation infeasible at scale
No zero-infrastructure tooling exists for semantic governance analysis without heavy deployment overhead
LLM inference latency risk from per-request client instantiation and batched parallel Azure AI Foundry calls
TF-IDF vectorizer refit on every request introduces unnecessary recomputation overhead per upload
LLM non-determinism risks producing non-auditable, inconsistent governance outputs without strict controls
BI administrators lack cross-report attribute consistency visibility across large multi-team PowerBI tenants
problem_statement.impact: Governance analysts spend excessive manual effort reconciling PowerBI metadata, leading to delayed compliance reporting and undetected data inconsistencies across teams
problem_statement.root_cause: Absence of automated semantic tooling that operates without infrastructure overhead, combined with inherent LLM non-determinism and naming convention fragmentation across BI teams

proposed_solution.summary: Browser-deployable SPA with Python monolithic pipeline combining TF-IDF, Jaccard, Levenshtein, and LLM semantic scoring to auto-generate Excel governance reports from PowerBI metadata uploads
key_differentiators: Hybrid three-stage scoring pipeline combining TF-IDF, Jaccard, Levenshtein, and LLM semantic analysis
Zero-infrastructure SPA deployment requiring no server provisioning, login, or persistent state
Meta Llama 3.3 70B via Azure AI Foundry with temperature 0.1 enforcing deterministic auditable outputs
ThreadPoolExecutor parallelised LLM batching at 25 pairs per call with retry and backoff logic
Unicode normalisation and input sanitisation applied pre-scoring to guarantee data quality and security
proposed_solution.approach: Upload-process-export pipeline: user uploads PowerBI metadata Excel/CSV, backend performs in-memory hybrid scoring, LLM validates semantic matches, Excel governance report is returned for download

architecture.pattern: Single-Page Application with monolithic Python processing pipeline and zero persistent server-side state
architecture.frontend: Bootstrap 5.3.3 SPA with drag-and-drop upload and Excel export download
architecture.backend: Python monolithic server.py pipeline with scikit-learn and Azure AI Foundry LLM integration
architecture.ai_layer: Meta Llama 3.3 70B Instruct via Azure AI Foundry with batched parallel inference
architecture.data_store: In-memory per-request attribute dictionary; no persistent database
architecture.hosting: Browser-deployable zero-infrastructure static hosting with Python backend process

components.label: User / Client
components.name: Web Browser Governance Client
components.role: Entry point for metadata upload and governance report download interactions
components.technology: Web Browser, REST client, HTML5 File API

components.label: SPA Frontend
components.name: Bootstrap SPA Governance Interface
components.role: Renders drag-and-drop upload UI, progress feedback, and triggers Excel report download
components.technology: Bootstrap 5.3.3, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Purple design system

components.label: Python Pipeline
components.name: Monolithic Python Governance Processing Pipeline
components.role: Orchestrates full ingestion, normalisation, scoring, and report generation workflow

components.label: Input Sanitiser

components.role: Strips whitespace, lowercases, and Unicode-normalises all attribute strings before scoring

components.role: Computes local similarity scores for all attribute pairs before LLM semantic validation
components.technology: scikit-learn TF-IDF, character bi-gram to 4-gram, python-Levenshtein, Jaccard

components.label: LLM Orchestrator
components.name: Parallelised LLM Inference Orchestrator
components.role: Batches attribute pairs at 25 per call and dispatches parallel LLM requests with retry logic

components.label: Azure AI Foundry
components.name: Azure AI Foundry LLM Endpoint
components.role: Hosts Meta Llama 3.3 70B Instruct and returns deterministic JSON semantic match scores
components.technology: Azure AI Foundry, AzureOpenAI client, Meta Llama 3.3 70B Instruct, temperature 0.1

components.label: Report Generator
components.name: Excel Governance Report Generator
components.role: Assembles final scored attribute matches into downloadable Excel governance report

data_flow: User drags and drops PowerBI metadata Excel or CSV file onto the SPA landing interface in the browser
SPA sends multipart HTTP POST with the uploaded file to the Python monolithic pipeline backend endpoint
Python pipeline parses the file into an in-memory attribute dictionary keyed by report name to field, measure, and dimension string lists
Input sanitiser applies Unicode normalisation, whitespace stripping, and lowercasing to all extracted attribute strings
Local scorer fits TF-IDF vectorizer on the request corpus and computes TF-IDF cosine, Jaccard, and Levenshtein scores for all attribute pairs
Candidate pairs exceeding local similarity threshold are batched at 25 pairs per call and dispatched to Azure AI Foundry via parallelised ThreadPoolExecutor
Meta Llama 3.3 70B Instruct returns strict JSON semantic match scores with temperature 0.1; retry and backoff handles transient Azure failures
Report generator merges local and LLM scores, assembles ranked duplicate and similarity findings, and returns downloadable Excel governance report to the browser

data: Excel XLSX input parsing via Pandas
infrastructure: Azure AI Foundry managed LLM endpoint

non_functional.scalability: Stateless per-request processing with ThreadPoolExecutor parallelism scales horizontally; LLM batching at 25 pairs manages Azure API rate limits
non_functional.security: Zero persistent state minimises attack surface; input sanitisation prevents injection; no authentication data stored server-side
non_functional.availability: Azure AI Foundry retry and backoff logic ensures resilience against transient LLM endpoint failures during governance report generation
non_functional.performance: Hybrid local scoring pre-filters pairs before LLM calls, reducing Azure AI Foundry invocations and targeting sub-5-minute report generation
non_functional.compliance: Deterministic LLM outputs via temperature 0.1 and JSON-only prompts produce auditable, reproducible governance results supporting data compliance requirements

deliverables: SPA scaffold with Bootstrap 5.3.3 drag-and-drop upload and purple design system implemented
Python pipeline skeleton with Excel and CSV parsing into in-memory attribute dictionary
Input sanitisation module with Unicode normalisation, whitespace stripping, and lowercasing
Azure AI Foundry account provisioned and Meta Llama 3.3 70B Instruct endpoint validated
TF-IDF character bi-gram to 4-gram vectorizer with Jaccard and Levenshtein hybrid scoring engine
LLM orchestrator with ThreadPoolExecutor batching at 25 pairs per call and retry backoff logic
Strict JSON-only prompt templates with temperature 0.1 enforcing deterministic LLM outputs
Excel governance report generator assembling ranked duplicate and similarity findings via openpyxl
Performance tuning of local scoring threshold to minimise unnecessary LLM API calls
End-to-end determinism validation suite testing JSON parse success rate across 1000 requests
Responsive SPA breakpoint refinement at 768px and 480px with cross-browser compatibility testing
User acceptance testing with Data Governance Analysts and BI Platform Administrators on real estates

risks.risk: Azure AI Foundry LLM latency spikes cause governance report generation to exceed acceptable time thresholds
risks.mitigation: Implement retry with exponential backoff, cap ThreadPoolExecutor at max_workers=2, and pre-filter pairs with local scoring to reduce LLM call volume

risks.risk: TF-IDF vectorizer refit per request introduces significant CPU overhead for very large PowerBI estates
risks.mitigation: Profile vectorizer fit time against realistic estate sizes and introduce request-scoped caching or incremental fitting if thresholds are breached

risks.risk: LLM returns malformed JSON despite strict prompt constraints, breaking report generation pipeline
risks.mitigation: Wrap all LLM response parsing in try-except with fallback to local-only scoring and log all parse failures for prompt refinement

risks.risk: Large metadata file uploads cause browser memory pressure or HTTP timeout in zero-infrastructure deployment
risks.mitigation: Enforce client-side file size validation in SPA, implement streaming file parsing in Python pipeline, and document supported estate size limits

risks.risk: Azure AI Foundry API rate limits throttle parallel LLM calls for large attribute pair volumes
risks.mitigation: Enforce max_workers=2 cap, implement token-bucket rate limiting in orchestrator, and provide user-facing progress feedback during processing

assumptions: Users have access to a modern web browser and can export PowerBI metadata as Excel or CSV without additional tooling
Azure AI Foundry subscription with Meta Llama 3.3 70B Instruct endpoint is provisioned and accessible from the backend host
PowerBI metadata exports contain consistent enough structure for Pandas to parse report name, field, measure, and dimension columns
Governance analysts accept sub-5-minute processing time as acceptable for estates up to a defined maximum attribute count
No authentication or multi-user session management is required as the tool operates as a single-user stateless utility
open_questions: What is the maximum PowerBI estate size in attribute count that must be supported within the 5-minute performance target?
Should the TF-IDF vectorizer similarity threshold for LLM escalation be configurable by the user or fixed in the pipeline?
Is there a requirement to persist or audit governance report outputs server-side for compliance record-keeping purposes?
What fallback behaviour is expected when Azure AI Foundry is unavailable — local-only scoring report or hard failure?
Are there specific PowerBI metadata export column schemas that must be supported, or should the tool handle arbitrary column naming?
